# Formula registry

Source: `data/formulas/formulas.toml`. Status: STANDARD = definition / textbook identity, MODEL = approximation with stated validity, RULE = rule of thumb. Equations use KiCad markup (`_{}` subscript, `^{}` superscript, `~{}` overbar).

## `ohm` - STANDARD

`V = I·R`

- variables: V voltage [V], I current [A], R resistance [Ω]
- assumptions: linear resistor
- source: definition

## `power` - STANDARD

`P = V·I = I^{2}R = V^{2}/R`

- variables: P power [W], V [V], I [A], R [Ω]
- assumptions: DC or RMS quantities; resistive load for the last two forms
- source: Joule's law

## `cap_energy` - STANDARD

`E = C·V^{2}/2`

- variables: E energy [J], C capacitance [F], V voltage [V]
- assumptions: ideal, voltage-independent C (class II MLCC capacitance drops with DC bias)
- source: definition

## `ind_energy` - STANDARD

`E = L·I^{2}/2`

- variables: E energy [J], L inductance [H], I current [A]
- assumptions: linear, non-saturated inductor
- source: definition

## `rc_tau` - STANDARD

`τ = R·C`

- variables: τ time constant [s], R [Ω], C [F]
- assumptions: first-order RC; 63.2 % of step after τ, 99.3 % after 5τ
- source: first-order step response

## `rc_fc` - STANDARD

`f_{c} = 1/(2π·R·C)`

- variables: f_{c} -3 dB frequency [Hz], R [Ω], C [F]
- assumptions: first-order RC, ideal source/load
- source: first-order transfer function
- checked by: `test_eng.Physics.test_rc_lc`

## `lc_f0` - STANDARD

`f_{0} = 1/(2π·√(L·C))`

- variables: f_{0} resonance [Hz], L [H], C [F]
- assumptions: lossless LC
- source: resonance condition X_{L} = X_{C}
- checked by: `test_eng.Physics.test_rc_lc`

## `xc` - STANDARD

`X_{C} = 1/(2π·f·C)`

- variables: X_{C} reactance [Ω], f [Hz], C [F]
- assumptions: ideal capacitor (no ESR/ESL)
- source: definition

## `xl` - STANDARD

`X_{L} = 2π·f·L`

- variables: X_{L} reactance [Ω], f [Hz], L [H]
- assumptions: ideal inductor
- source: definition

## `z_complex` - STANDARD

`Z = R + jX,  |Z| = √(R^{2}+X^{2}),  φ = atan(X/R)`

- variables: Z impedance [Ω], R resistance, X reactance [Ω], φ phase [rad]
- assumptions: sinusoidal steady state
- source: phasor analysis

## `divider` - STANDARD

`V_{out} = V_{in}·R2/(R1+R2)`

- variables: V_{in}, V_{out} [V]; R1 top, R2 bottom [Ω]
- assumptions: unloaded output (R_{load} >> R2)
- source: Kirchhoff

## `current_divider` - STANDARD

`I_{1} = I·R2/(R1+R2)`

- variables: I total [A], I_{1} current in R1 [A]
- assumptions: two parallel resistors
- source: Kirchhoff

## `inv_amp` - STANDARD

`A_{v} = −R_{f}/R_{in}`

- variables: A_{v} voltage gain [V/V], R_{f} feedback, R_{in} input [Ω]
- assumptions: ideal op-amp (infinite open-loop gain); real parts need GBW, stability, offset checks
- source: virtual-ground analysis

## `noninv_amp` - STANDARD

`A_{v} = 1 + R_{f}/R_{g}`

- variables: A_{v} [V/V], R_{f} feedback, R_{g} to ground [Ω]
- assumptions: ideal op-amp
- source: virtual-short analysis

## `diff_amp` - STANDARD

`V_{out} = (R2/R1)·(V_{2} − V_{1})`

- variables: R1 input, R2 feedback/ground [Ω]
- assumptions: matched ratios R2/R1 = R4/R3; CMRR limited by resistor matching
- source: superposition

## `sum_amp` - STANDARD

`V_{out} = −R_{f}·(V_{1}/R1 + V_{2}/R2)`

- variables: V_{1}, V_{2} inputs [V], R1, R2, R_{f} [Ω]
- assumptions: ideal op-amp, inverting summer
- source: virtual-ground superposition

## `ina` - STANDARD

`G = 1 + 2R/R_{G}`

- variables: G gain [V/V], R internal first-stage resistor, R_{G} gain resistor [Ω]
- assumptions: classic 3-op-amp INA with unity-gain difference stage; check the actual part's G equation
- source: 3-op-amp instrumentation amplifier analysis

## `integrator` - STANDARD

`V_{out} = −(1/RC)·∫V_{in}dt`

- variables: R input [Ω], C feedback [F]
- assumptions: ideal op-amp; needs DC path (R across C) in practice
- source: virtual-ground analysis

## `differentiator` - STANDARD

`V_{out} = −RC·dV_{in}/dt`

- variables: R feedback [Ω], C input [F]
- assumptions: ideal; practical circuits add series R / parallel C to limit HF gain
- source: virtual-ground analysis

## `tia` - STANDARD

`V_{out} = −I_{in}·R_{f}`

- variables: I_{in} input current [A], R_{f} [Ω]
- assumptions: ideal; C_{f} required for stability with real input capacitance
- source: virtual-ground analysis

## `tia_cf` - MODEL

`C_{f} ≈ √(C_{in}/(2π·R_{f}·GBW))`

- variables: C_{in} total input capacitance [F], GBW [Hz]
- assumptions: single-pole op-amp; gives ~45° phase margin (Butterworth-like); verify by simulation
- source: J. Graeme, Photodiode Amplifiers (1996); common TI/ADI application notes

## `db_v` - STANDARD

`G_{dB} = 20·log_{10}(V_{2}/V_{1})`

- variables: voltage ratio
- assumptions: same impedance for power interpretation
- source: definition
- checked by: `test_eng.Conversions.test_temperature_db`

## `db_p` - STANDARD

`G_{dB} = 10·log_{10}(P_{2}/P_{1})`

- variables: power ratio
- assumptions: 
- source: definition

## `noise_r` - STANDARD

`e_{n} = √(4·k·T·R)`

- variables: e_{n} [V/√Hz], k 1.380649e-23 J/K, T [K], R [Ω]
- assumptions: thermal (Johnson) noise only
- source: Nyquist 1928
- checked by: `test_eng.Physics.test_thermal_noise_1k`

## `noise_int` - STANDARD

`V_{n,rms} = e_{n}·√(ENBW),  ENBW = (π/2)·f_{c}`

- variables: ENBW equivalent noise bandwidth [Hz]
- assumptions: white noise; ENBW factor π/2 for a single-pole low-pass
- source: noise-bandwidth definition

## `slew_fpbw` - STANDARD

`f_{max} = SR/(2π·V_{p})`

- variables: SR slew rate [V/s], V_{p} peak output [V]
- assumptions: full-power sine without slew distortion
- source: dV/dt of a sine

## `rtd` - STANDARD

`R(T) = R_{0}(1 + A·T + B·T^{2})`

- variables: R_{0} 100/1000 Ω at 0 °C, A 3.9083e-3, B -5.775e-7, T [°C]
- assumptions: 0..850 °C (IEC 60751; below 0 °C an extra C term applies)
- source: IEC 60751 Callendar-Van Dusen coefficients

## `ntc` - MODEL

`R(T) = R_{25}·e^{B(1/T − 1/T_{25})}`

- variables: B constant [K], T absolute [K], T_{25} = 298.15 K
- assumptions: Beta model, ~±1 °C over a limited range; use Steinhart-Hart for precision
- source: thermistor Beta equation

## `buck_d` - STANDARD

`D = V_{out}/V_{in}`

- variables: D duty cycle
- assumptions: ideal buck, continuous conduction mode (CCM)
- source: volt-second balance

## `buck_ripple` - STANDARD

`ΔI_{L} = (V_{in} − V_{out})·D/(f_{sw}·L)`

- variables: ΔI_{L} peak-peak inductor ripple [A], f_{sw} [Hz], L [H]
- assumptions: ideal buck, CCM
- source: inductor V = L·di/dt

## `boost_d` - STANDARD

`D = 1 − V_{in}/V_{out}`

- variables: D duty cycle
- assumptions: ideal boost, CCM
- source: volt-second balance

## `buckboost_d` - STANDARD

`V_{out} = −V_{in}·D/(1 − D)`

- variables: inverting buck-boost output
- assumptions: ideal, CCM
- source: volt-second balance

## `ldo_pd` - STANDARD

`P_{D} = (V_{in} − V_{out})·I_{out} + V_{in}·I_{Q}`

- variables: I_{Q} quiescent/ground current [A]
- assumptions: linear regulator
- source: power balance

## `efficiency` - STANDARD

`η = P_{out}/P_{in}`

- variables: η efficiency (0..1)
- assumptions: 
- source: definition

## `mos_cond` - STANDARD

`P_{cond} = I_{rms}^{2}·R_{DS(on)}`

- variables: R_{DS(on)} at actual T_{j} and V_{GS} (rises ~1.5-2x hot)
- assumptions: MOSFET fully enhanced
- source: Joule loss

## `mos_sw` - MODEL

`P_{sw} ≈ V·I·(t_{r} + t_{f})·f_{sw}/2`

- variables: t_{r}, t_{f} switching transition times [s]
- assumptions: hard switching, linear V/I overlap; ignores Q_{rr}, C_{oss} losses
- source: first-order switching-loss model

## `tj` - MODEL

`T_{j} = T_{a} + P·θ_{JA}`

- variables: θ_{JA} junction-ambient [K/W] (board dependent!)
- assumptions: steady state; θ_{JA} from a JEDEC test board rarely matches your board
- source: thermal Ohm's law

## `ipc2221` - MODEL

`I = k·ΔT^{0.44}·A^{0.725}`

- variables: I [A], ΔT rise [°C], A cross-section [mil²], k 0.048 ext / 0.024 int
- assumptions: legacy IPC-2221 chart fit; IPC-2152 supersedes; depends on board, planes, airflow
- source: IPC-2221 design chart curve fit (widely published)
- checked by: `test_eng.Physics.test_copper`

## `via_r` - MODEL

`R_{via} = ρ·t_{b}/(π·(d + t_{p})·t_{p})`

- variables: t_{b} board thickness, d finished hole, t_{p} plating [m]
- assumptions: thin cylindrical barrel; ignores pads/spreading
- source: resistance of a tube

## `cu_r` - STANDARD

`R = ρ·L/(W·t) = R_{□}·L/W`

- variables: ρ 1.72e-8 Ωm (20 °C), R_{□} sheet resistance [Ω/sq]
- assumptions: uniform DC current; +0.39 %/K
- source: definition
- checked by: `test_eng.Physics.test_copper`

## `z0_lc` - STANDARD

`Z_{0} = √(L'/C')`

- variables: L', C' per-unit-length inductance [H/m] and capacitance [F/m]
- assumptions: lossless line
- source: telegrapher's equations

## `gamma` - STANDARD

`Γ = (Z_{L} − Z_{0})/(Z_{L} + Z_{0})`

- variables: Γ reflection coefficient, Z_{L} load, Z_{0} line [Ω]
- assumptions: 
- source: definition
- checked by: `test_eng.RF.test_gamma_vswr`

`RL = −20·log_{10}|Γ|`

- variables: RL [dB] (positive number); S11 [dB] = −RL
- assumptions: 
- source: definition
- checked by: `test_eng.RF.test_gamma_vswr`

## `vswr` - STANDARD

`VSWR = (1 + |Γ|)/(1 − |Γ|)`

- variables: voltage standing wave ratio
- assumptions: 
- source: definition
- checked by: `test_eng.RF.test_gamma_vswr`

## `lambda` - STANDARD

`λ = c/(f·√ε_{eff})`

- variables: c 299 792 458 m/s, f [Hz], ε_{eff} effective permittivity
- assumptions: ε_{eff} = 1 for free space
- source: definition
- checked by: `test_eng.RF.test_wavelength`

## `tpd` - STANDARD

`t_{d} = L·√ε_{eff}/c`

- variables: L line length [m]
- assumptions: TEM / quasi-TEM line
- source: definition

## `dipole` - RULE

`L_{m} ≈ 143/f_{MHz}`

- variables: L_{m} total half-wave dipole length [m]
- assumptions: thin wire in free space, ≈0.95·λ/2 end-effect shortening; first estimate only
- source: classic amateur-radio approximation (ARRL)

## `monopole` - RULE

`L_{m} ≈ 71.5/f_{MHz}  (λ/4 = 75/f_{MHz})`

- variables: L_{m} quarter-wave monopole [m]
- assumptions: over a large ground plane; 75/f is the free-space λ/4, 71.5/f includes ≈0.95 shortening
- source: half of the dipole approximation

## `microstrip` - MODEL

`Z_{0}(W,h,ε_{r},t)  Hammerstad-Jensen`

- variables: W width, h dielectric height, t copper thickness [mm], ε_{r}
- assumptions: quasi-static, ~1 % for 0.1 < W/h < 10; ignores solder mask (lowers Z_{0} a few Ω)
- source: E. Hammerstad, O. Jensen, IEEE MTT-S 1980
- checked by: `test_eng.RF.test_microstrip_reference`

## `stripline` - MODEL

`Z_{0} = (η_{0}/(4√ε_{r}))·K(k)/K(k'),  k = sech(πW/2b)`

- variables: b ground-to-ground spacing, W width [mm]
- assumptions: centred, zero-thickness strip (Cohn 1954)
- source: S. Cohn, IRE Trans. MTT 1954; Pozar, Microwave Engineering
- checked by: `test_eng.RF.test_stripline_reference`

## `cpwg` - MODEL

`Z_{0} = 60π/√ε_{eff} · 1/(K(k1)/K(k1') + K(k3)/K(k3'))`

- variables: k1 = W/(W+2G), k3 = tanh(πW/4h)/tanh(π(W+2G)/4h)
- assumptions: zero thickness, infinitely wide top grounds, via-stitched
- source: B. Wadell, Transmission Line Design Handbook (1991)
- checked by: `test_eng.RF.test_cpwg_monotonic`

## `diff_ms` - MODEL

`Z_{diff} ≈ 2Z_{0}·(1 − 0.48·e^{−0.96·S/h})`

- variables: S edge gap, h dielectric height
- assumptions: edge-coupled microstrip, rough (±10 %) - use a field solver for production
- source: IPC-2141 approximation

## `knee` - RULE

`f_{knee} ≈ 0.35/t_{r}`

- variables: t_{r} 10-90 % rise time [s]
- assumptions: single-pole edge; 0.5/t_{r} is also quoted
- source: Johnson & Graham, High-Speed Digital Design

## `patch` - MODEL

`W = c/(2f)·√(2/(ε_{r}+1)),  L = c/(2f√ε_{eff}) − 2ΔL`

- variables: ΔL fringing extension (Hammerstad)
- assumptions: rectangular patch, transmission-line model; detuned by enclosure, feed, tolerance
- source: C. Balanis, Antenna Theory, ch. 14

## `lmatch_q` - STANDARD

`Q = √(R_{H}/R_{L} − 1)`

- variables: R_{H}, R_{L} higher / lower resistance [Ω]
- assumptions: lossless L network, single frequency
- source: L-network design

## `wilkinson` - STANDARD

`λ/4 arms Z = √2·Z_{0},  R = 2Z_{0}`

- variables: equal split, Z_{0} port impedance
- assumptions: narrow-band (λ/4 sections)
- source: Pozar, Microwave Engineering

## `i2c_rp` - STANDARD

`R_{p,min} = (V_{DD} − V_{OL,max})/I_{OL},  R_{p,max} = t_{r}/(0.8473·C_{b})`

- variables: t_{r} max rise time, C_{b} bus capacitance
- assumptions: standard/fast/fast+ mode limits from the I2C specification
- source: NXP UM10204 I2C-bus specification, section 7.1

## `xtal_cl` - STANDARD

`C1 = C2 ≈ 2·(C_{L} − C_{stray})`

- variables: C_{L} crystal load capacitance, C_{stray} ~2-5 pF
- assumptions: Pierce oscillator, C_{L} = C1·C2/(C1+C2) + C_{stray}
- source: series combination of load capacitors

## `adc_lsb` - STANDARD

`LSB = V_{ref}/2^{N}`

- variables: N resolution [bits]
- assumptions: ideal ADC, unipolar full scale
- source: definition

## `adc_snr` - STANDARD

`SNR_{ideal} = 6.02·N + 1.76 dB`

- variables: N bits
- assumptions: full-scale sine, quantisation noise only
- source: quantisation noise LSB/√12

## `nyquist` - STANDARD

`f_{s} > 2·f_{max}`

- variables: f_{s} sample rate, f_{max} highest signal content
- assumptions: practical anti-alias filters need margin (f_{s} ≈ 2.5-10× f_{max})
- source: Nyquist-Shannon sampling theorem

## `shunt` - STANDARD

`V_{sense} = I·R_{s},  P_{Rs} = I^{2}·R_{s}`

- variables: R_{s} shunt resistance [Ω]
- assumptions: Kelvin connection removes trace resistance
- source: Ohm's law
